answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the economy of AI agents deploys a proof-of-personhood mechanism anchored in a verifiable delay function (VDF). An attacker must compute a VDF iteratively—mining copper from the ocean of synthetic identities—before a human ridge of consensus validators accepts the resulting credential. This imposes a prohibitive computational and temporal cost, binding agents to scarce, humanity-backed reputation instead of scalable fake accounts.
